P001.text: Act on the reported 19 late starts among 74 bookings over six weeks and on competing explanations for why calendar availability did not translate into timely starts.

P002.text: Treat delayed returns, unfinished cleaning, inaccurate availability updates and delayed collection as hypotheses, not established causes.

P003.text: Assume records can be linked to equipment and bookings; verify this first.

P004.text: Distinguish scheduled start, physical return, cleaning completion, readiness for collection, collection and actual work start.

P005.text: Establish what the reported 'late start' measures and use the existing lateness rule, or agree one before comparison if none exists.

P006.text: During days 1–4, assemble booking-level timelines from the calendar and separate return, cleaning and collection logs.

P007.text: Review all 19 reported late cases and use the remaining bookings to check whether suspected problems also occur without lateness.

P008.text: Preserve missing entries and uncertain matches explicitly.

P009.text: For each material claim, record who observed what, when it was recorded, whether the source had direct access, and whether it copied another record.

P010.text: Seek independently grounded checks through existing crew and depot accounts or contemporaneous records where available; ask about specific events before presenting a proposed explanation.

P011.text: During days 5–8, prospectively check disputed handoff points within existing staffing, using separate firsthand observations where feasible.

P012.text: Reconcile conflicting timestamps, definitions and equipment identities without forcing agreement.

P013.text: By days 9–10, compare candidate changes against the corroborated failure patterns, their frequency and delay burden, operational feasibility and possible effects on other crews.

P014.text: Conditional candidates include a turnaround allowance for verified return-to-ready delays, a readiness confirmation before calendar release for verified status errors, or a collection handoff rule for verified collection failures.

P015.text: Select one narrowly scoped, reversible trial by the two-week deadline; do not combine changes whose effects could not be distinguished.

P016.text: Look for independent agreement or disagreement about the same equipment, booking and handoff.

P017.text: For example, a return entry and a separately recorded firsthand observation could support that equipment arrived after the next scheduled start; a cleaning entry and an independent readiness check could support that cleaning remained incomplete at that time.

P018.text: Calendar availability alone does not establish physical readiness.

P019.text: Record contradictions, unsupported intervals and missing coverage alongside supported sequences.

P020.text: Count supported patterns across bookings and note whether similar patterns occur among timely bookings.

P021.text: For the selected trial, prospectively observe late-start frequency and delay duration, readiness and collection times, completed or displaced bookings, and any added workload or unmet cleaning requirements.

P022.text: Convergence among credible sources with independent access increases support for the specific corroborated timing or status feature.

P023.text: Repeated supported sequences can justify prioritizing a corresponding change for trial, especially when their timing plausibly explains the delay and comparison bookings strengthen that explanation.

P024.text: Favor the feasible change addressing the largest credible, avoidable delay burden without purchasing equipment or adding staff.

P025.text: Contradictions lower confidence and direct follow-up toward the disputed handoff.

P026.text: If no explanation has adequate independent support by the deadline, select a limited readiness-confirmation trial primarily to resolve uncertainty, explicitly leaving its delay-reduction benefit unestablished.

P027.text: Compare trial outcomes with comparable baseline bookings, accounting for equipment, crew and demand differences; improvement supports continued testing but does not alone establish causation.

P028.text: Separate logs are not necessarily independent: they may share an author, copied timestamps, clock errors or assumptions.

P029.text: Retrospective accounts may share a narrative, and missingness may be concentrated in busy or delayed periods.

P030.text: Absence of an entry does not prove that an event failed to occur.

P031.text: Corroborated timing does not by itself establish the cause of lateness, and readiness, collection and work start are different events.

P032.text: Stop treating a disputed feature as established when source dependence, poor access or unresolved contradictions undermine it; retain competing explanations.

P033.text: Before trial launch, specify its duration, comparable bookings, success criterion and acceptable workload and access effects.

P034.text: Stop or revise the trial if it compromises required cleaning, safe use or essential crew access, or requires extra staffing.

P035.text: If too few comparable bookings occur, extend observation within existing resources rather than claim success or failure from inadequate evidence.
